sara_cs: Quick heartbeat check for AcmeCorp onboarding — I noticed a spike in 5xxs and timeouts yesterday afternoon. Snapshot below, can anyone pick this up? @james_reliability @omar_onboard :eyes:

opsbot: [ALERT] AcmeCorp — 5xx spike detected 2026-03-19 14:02–14:18 UTC. Total 5xx: 78. Top path: /v1/generate (count=48).

james_reliability: Saw the alert, digging in now. Initial look: a cluster of long-sequence requests causing backpressure + batch timeouts. Sharing the query I used to pull counts:
```sql
SELECT path, status, count(*) AS cnt
FROM request_logs
WHERE account_id = 'acme-123' AND ts >= '2026-03-19T14:00:00Z'
GROUP BY path, status
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

ellie_se: From the customer side they ran an onboarding sync that kicked off ~14:01 UTC. They confirm payloads with sequence_length ~3500–4200 tokens and high concurrency (10x usual). That explains the timeouts.

omar_onboard: I pinged the Acme eng lead — they did increase parallelism to speed things up. They're rolling back concurrency now and will adopt smaller batch sizes per our guidance. I'll coordinate the config changes.

sara_cs: Action items: 1) temporary per-account routing to lower batch size; 2) set a soft rate-limit on their API key to smooth bursts (suggest 80rpm); 3) follow up in the next check-in. Who can own the routing change? :clipboard:

james_reliability: I will apply a temporary canary policy. Patch: set `batch_limit=8` for account acme-123 and add a 60s rollout window. Command I ran (k8s config snippet):
```yaml
- match: account: acme-123
  override:
    runtime.batch_limit: 8
    routing.priority: canary
```
ETA ~30m to be live. I'll monitor error rate and latencies.

ellie_se: Also saw a secondary issue: 429s on /v1/embeddings — count ~43 in the same window. Those look like client-side spikes too (many small embedding calls).

sara_cs: Noted. Preliminary weekly summary for internal doc: 5xx spike = 78 (mainly /v1/generate), timeouts = 52 (long sequences + batch timeouts), rate limits/429 = 43 (mostly /v1/embeddings). Rough spend impact ~+$120/day for the burst window. I'm updating the account notes and moving renewal risk from "low" to "medium" until we confirm stability.

omar_onboard: I'll send them a short guidance doc with recommended concurrency, backoff, and an example retry/backoff snippet. cc @ellie_se

james_reliability: Policy applied and healthy so far. Monitoring link: https://redwood.internal/status/alerts/2265432100 (internal). Plan: revert policy after 6h if error rate remains within baseline.

sara_cs: Perfect, thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll include this in the weekly account health email to CS and AMs with the bullet summary and next steps.

end of thread
